Judy Van Wyck, Chairperson Africana Studies supports the Department of Sociology in their proposal for a Social Justice and Civic Responsibilities Minor.
The AAF Faculty have several concerns that can be summarized in the following statement.
While we support a minor in social justice, we believe the present state of Africana Studies reflects the results of systematic lack of support, marginalization and institutionalized neglect.
Without the adequate funding, staffing and support that is necessary for any area of study to carry out basic administrative and academic functions, successful and progressive development is impeded.
Complexly, Africana Studies has "partnered" in the past with other departments in well-meaning projects.
Often the result has been that the other departments receive the recognition and subsequent funding while Africana Studies remains perpetually without recognition of its contributions and thereby unable to garner the funding and support necessary for progress.
We have seen this pattern repeated too many times and we are hoping that these kinds of institutional blocks to true equity and social justice can be dismantled.

We would like our support of the Social Justice and Civic Responsiblities minor to strengthen increased support of Africana Studies, specifically, adequate funding, staffing and departmental status.
Toward that end, we conditionally support Sociology in the effort to establish a very important minor, the Social Justice and Civic Responsibilities minor, and even expect our relationship with Sociology to model social justice by noting the following concerns: A.) This Minor should not be seen as a segue away from the Africana Studies Major/Minor, but rather a field of study that is compatible with the academic goals of Africana Studies.
B.) Africana Studies will be able to "count" involvement in the Social Justice minor as credit in our overall assessment C.) Africana Studies maintains rightful decision -making over hiring of Faculty (especially adjunct Faculty) to teach the courses that are solely designated as AAF.
D.) The Sociology Department will keep Africana Studies informed of decisions about the minor that will impact Africana Studies.

Judy Van Wyck, Chairperson Africana Studies supports the Department of Sociology in their proposal for a Social Justice and Civic Responsibilities Minor.
The AAF Faculty have several concerns that can be summarized in the following statement.
While we support a minor in social justi ce, we believe the present state of Africana Studies reflects the results of systematic lack of support, marginalization and institutionalized neglect.

Without the adequate funding, staffing and support that is necessary for any area of study to carry out basic administrative and academic functions, successful and progressive development is impeded.
Complexly, Africana Studies has "partnered" in the past with other departments in well-meaning projects.
Often the result has been that the other departments receive the recognition and subsequent funding while Africana Studies remains perpetually without recognition of its contributions and thereby unable to garner the funding and support necessary for progress.
We have seen this pattern repeated too many times and we are hoping that these kinds of institutional blocks to true equity and social justice can be dismantled.
We would like our support of the Social Justice and Civic Responsiblities minor to strengthen increased support of Africana Studies, specifically, adequate funding, staffing and departmental status.

Toward that end, we conditionally support Sociology in the effort to establish a very important minor, the Social Justice and Civic Responsibilities minor, and even expect our relationship with Sociology to model social justice by noting the following concerns: A.) This Minor should not be seen as a segue away from the Africana Studies Major/Minor, but rather a field of study that is compatible with the academic goals of Africana Studies.
B.) Africana Studies will be able to "count" involvement in the Social Justice minor as credit in our overall assessment C.) Africana Studies maintains rightful decision -making over hiring of Faculty (especially adjunct Faculty) to teach the courses that are solely designated as AAF.
D.) The Sociology Department will keep Africana Studies informed of decisions about the minor that will impact Africana Studies.
Sincerely, Dr.
